newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GERMAN FIRM LAUNCH EBRD HUNGARY TURNAROUND SCHEME.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN FIRM LAUNCH EBRD HUNGARY TURNAROUND SCHEME.

text.p: German corporate restructuring company Sandtner Hamilton Management GmbH said on Thursday it had identified three Hungarian firms which could be the first to benefit from the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)'s Hungarian Special Restructuring Programme.
The programme, which the EBRD announced in December, involves a 30 million Ecu facility to finance the restructuring of viable under-performing medium-sized Hungarian companies.
It will provide higher-risk equity finance, turnaround management expertise, technical cooperation and a framework to promote debt and operational restructuring to viable companies.
Up to 30 million Ecu of equity finance will be invested in a portfolio of 10 to 15 Hungarian companies, mainly local banks and managerial buyouts, during the seven-year life of the programme.
"We have selected a short list of three companies," SHM's CEO Josef Sandtner told reporters on Thursday, but declined to name the companies.
"We are convinced that...we will be able to help these companies to restructure and show a significant return on investment in three to five years," he said.
The European Union's PHARE programme is supporting the EBRD investment by providing 5.4 million Ecu in technical cooperation funds.

Sandtner said SHM would top up the EBRD investment with "a significant amount" of its own funds, adding that the PHARE assistance will allow SHM to undertake due-diligence and finalise pre-investment restructuring transactions.
